AIM.1.description: flag_out flip compares the disagreement count against the counter's sizing limit CNT_MAX (the assert time) instead of the target for the pending direction, so the release direction is forgotten
AIM.1.reason: With the default parameters (ASSERT > RELEASE), a release attempt clears the counter at RELEASE_CLKS-1 and never reaches ASSERT_CLKS-1. Once flag_out is high, it never goes low again, even when flag_in stays low indefinitely.

AIM.2.description: The disagreement counter's clear-on-qualify limit uses CNT_MAX instead of the selected target, so the count is not restarted on the edge a release qualifies
AIM.2.reason: When flag_out releases and flag_in goes high again on the very next clock, the counter keeps counting up from RELEASE_CLKS. flag_out then asserts after only ASSERT_CLKS-RELEASE_CLKS clocks of high input instead of ASSERT_CLKS.
AIM.2.withdrawn: same fault as AIM.17: the count is not restarted on the edge a release qualifies; the next qualification differs by one clock

AIM.3.description: The restart on agreement is applied only when flag_in is high, so an aborted assert attempt (flag_in back low while flag_out is low) leaves its partial count in place
AIM.3.reason: While flag_out is low, short high glitches on flag_in now add up across gaps instead of each restarting from zero. flag_out asserts once the glitches total ASSERT_CLKS clocks, even though no single pulse was that long: a false fault from switching-node pickup.

outcomes.detail: hit 4 SVA covers, the unmutated run 6

AIM.4.description: target_clks is written as a terminal count (qualification time minus one), while both compares still subtract one again, so every transition qualifies one clock early
AIM.4.reason: In both directions, flag_out now follows a steady new level of flag_in after ASSERT_CLKS-1 or RELEASE_CLKS-1 clocks of disagreement instead of ASSERT_CLKS or RELEASE_CLKS. The edge reaches the supervisor one clock early.

AIM.5.description: The clear-on-qualify restart only happens when a release qualifies; on the edge an assert qualifies the disagreement count is left at ASSERT_CLKS-1
AIM.5.reason: Suppose an assert qualifies and flag_in drops on the very next clock. The leftover count is already at or past RELEASE_CLKS-1, so flag_out releases after one low clock instead of RELEASE_CLKS clocks.

AIM.6.description: The flag_out flip compares the disagreement count against the release time for both directions, so the longer assert qualification is forgotten
AIM.6.reason: When flag_in goes high and stays high while flag_out is low, flag_out asserts after RELEASE_CLKS clocks (200 us) instead of ASSERT_CLKS (1 ms). An assert-going pulse between those two lengths now gets through.

AIM.7.description: The counter's clear-on-qualify limit is hard-coded to the release time, so during an assert attempt the count restarts every RELEASE_CLKS clocks and never reaches the assert target
AIM.7.reason: Once flag_out has released, a flag_in that holds high for any length of time never makes flag_out assert again, because the count is cleared at RELEASE_CLKS-1 before it reaches ASSERT_CLKS-1. Releases still qualify normally.

AIM.8.description: The flip rule is written for the assert direction only (flag_in high while flag_out low), so a qualified release never updates flag_out
AIM.8.reason: With RESET_VALUE=1, flag_out comes out of reset high and stays high however long flag_in holds low. The supervisor therefore never sees the fault clear.

AIM.9.description: The restart on agreement is applied only when flag_in is low, so an aborted release attempt (flag_in dips low while flag_out is high, then returns high) leaves its partial count in the disagreement counter
AIM.9.reason: With flag_out high, a low glitch on flag_in shorter than RELEASE_CLKS leaves the counter at the glitch length. A later low pulse then releases flag_out early, once the two together reach RELEASE_CLKS, instead of after RELEASE_CLKS continuous low clocks. Aborted asserts are still restarted correctly.

AIM.10.description: The flip compare adds a one-clock lookahead (counter+1) to make up for flag_out being registered, so flag_out flips one clock before the counter reaches its target and restarts
AIM.10.reason: Every transition with a target of 2 or more clocks shows up at flag_out one clock early. Because the counter only restarts on the next edge, an immediate reversal after an assert starts with the counter at ASSERT_CLKS-1, which is already past the release target, so flag_out flips straight back after one clock instead of waiting RELEASE_CLKS.

AIM.11.description: The disagreement counter measures flag_in against the fail-safe reset level RESET_VALUE instead of the believed state flag_out, so it counts time away from reset rather than time disagreeing with flag_out
AIM.11.reason: With the default RESET_VALUE=1, a low flag_in still qualifies and releases flag_out after RELEASE_CLKS. After that, a high flag_in clears the counter every clock instead of counting, so a real fault that holds flag_in high for any length of time never re-asserts flag_out.

outcomes.detail: hit 5 SVA covers, the unmutated run 6

AIM.12.description: The release qualification time is written as a terminal count (RELEASE_CLKS-1), but the assert time is not, so only a release qualifies one clock early
AIM.12.reason: After flag_in goes low and stays low while flag_out is high, flag_out falls after RELEASE_CLKS-1 clocks instead of RELEASE_CLKS. The assert timing does not change.

AIM.13.description: The disagreement counter only counts the release direction (flag_in low while flag_out is high), the move away from the high reset state, so an assert attempt never builds a count
AIM.13.reason: Once flag_out has released, flag_in going high and staying high leaves the counter at 0. The flip compare against ASSERT_CLKS-1 never passes, so flag_out never re-asserts.

AIM.14.description: The disagreement counter is preloaded to a full count in reset, so the first input level seen after reset is accepted without debouncing
AIM.14.reason: With flag_in low when rst_n is released, flag_out (reset high) falls on the first clock instead of after RELEASE_CLKS clocks of stable low. A glitch at that moment is passed straight through.

AIM.15.description: The disagreement counter only counts an assert attempt (flag_in high while flag_out is low), so the release direction never builds a count
AIM.15.reason: With the default fail-safe RESET_VALUE of 1, flag_out comes out of reset high and a healthy (low) flag_in never builds a count, so flag_out stays asserted forever and the supervisor never sees the fault clear.

AIM.16.description: flag_out is only allowed to flip when flag_in moves away from the fail-safe RESET_VALUE, so a return to the reset level (a re-asserted fault, with the default RESET_VALUE of 1) never updates flag_out
AIM.16.after: else if ((flag_in != RESET_VALUE) && (flag_in != flag_out) && (disagree_counter >= target_clks - 1'b1)) begin
AIM.16.reason: After the first qualified release, flag_out is low. A real fault that holds flag_in high for ASSERT_CLKS clocks or more lets the counter reach its target and restart, but flag_out never asserts again.

AIM.17.description: The clear-on-qualify restart only happens when an assert qualifies. On the edge a release qualifies, the disagreement count is left at RELEASE_CLKS-1
AIM.17.reason: If flag_in goes back high on the clock straight after a release flips flag_out low, the assert window starts from RELEASE_CLKS-1 instead of zero. flag_out then re-asserts after about ASSERT_CLKS-RELEASE_CLKS clocks instead of the full ASSERT_CLKS.
